transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because I'm having a really hard time focusing on my work. I'm a secondary school teacher, and I can sit down at my desk with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully intending to get through them. But within ten minutes or so, I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. My mind will be off thinking about three other things, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what’s right in front of me. It's just getting really frustrating.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with your focus?

Well, I'd say it's been noticeably worse for about 11 months now. That was right around the time the school changed our curriculum calendar. They also added these new after-school planning meetings, and ever since then, the trouble with my focus has just been a lot more obvious.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or focus when you were a child or teenager?

Yeah, I did. Honestly, even back in primary school, my report cards would always say things like... well, that I was bright but careless, or that I didn't finish my work unless I was closely supervised. And my parents were constantly finding worksheets just crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, it's definitely been an issue since I was a kid.
Over the past few months, have you been struggling with feeling consistently down, depressed, or hopeless?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I can't get my work done, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed or hopeless. It's more just annoying than anything else. My mood is generally fine.
Do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worry about everyday matters that feels difficult to control?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really have a lot of anxiety or worry about everyday things. Like I said, it's mostly just the frustration with my focus and getting things done, but I don't sit around worrying excessively.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) as the patient denies excessive, uncontrollable worry about everyday events.
